title: IBM Links Two Nighthawk r3 Chips To Make A 1,040-Qubit Quantum System
gist: IBM will ship the 520+-qubit Nighthawk r3 in 2027 and link two via l-couplers into a 1,040-qubit system, after on-chip reset made Nighthawk r2 run circuits up to 19x faster (34B+ circuits run). The modular, qLDPC-based path targets the fault-tolerant Starling (200 logical qubits) in 2029, backed by a CHIPS-funded Anderon quantum foundry and tighter quantum-classical HPC integration with AMD/Oak Ridge.

insights.claim: IBM's Nighthawk quantum processor (announced November 2025) has 120 qubits and moved from IBM's heavy-hex topology to a square-lattice architecture, improving qubit connectivity, crosstalk management and circuit depth.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Topology shift is IBM's lever for deeper circuits; track whether square-lattice benchmarks outpace heavy-hex Heron results.
insights.locator: A year ago this month, IBM announced Nighthawk

insights.claim: IBM's Nighthawk r2 QPU (unveiled September 2026) keeps 120 qubits but adds on-chip qubit reset, pushing throughput above 100,000 circuits per second.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Throughput, not just qubit count, is becoming a competitive metric for cloud quantum services.
insights.locator: In September, IBM unveiled Nighthawk r2

insights.claim: Users ran 8 billion circuits on IBM's Nighthawk r2 in its first three weeks of availability and more than 34 billion circuits since September 2026.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Usage volume signals real developer demand on IBM's quantum cloud, a proxy for platform stickiness.
insights.quote: In fact, in the first three weeks that this device was available, our users ran 8 billion circuits on it.
insights.locator: This is an extra physical qubit

insights.claim: IBM ran 7,500 gates on Nighthawk r2 19 times faster than would have been possible on Nighthawk r1, attributed to the on-chip reset capability.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Architectural tweaks (an extra reset qubit per programmable qubit) can yield order-of-magnitude speedups, lowering cost per useful computation.
insights.locator: Since September, more than 34 billion circuits

insights.claim: IBM plans to release Nighthawk r3 in 2027 with more than 520 qubits, support for 10,000 quantum operations, square-lattice connectivity and 10 chip-to-chip l-coupler interconnects.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: A 2027 delivery is a near-term checkpoint for whether IBM's roadmap stays on schedule.
insights.locator: Nighthawk r3 will scale to more 520 qubits

insights.claim: IBM will join two Nighthawk r3 processors via long-range couplers (l-couplers) into a single 1,040-qubit system for larger, more complex computations.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Modular multi-chip scaling is IBM's route past single-die limits; success de-risks its fault-tolerance timeline.
insights.quote: Connecting two Nighthawk r3 processors will create a 1,040-qubit system
insights.locator: Nighthawk r3 will scale to more 520 qubits

insights.claim: IBM argues speed matters as much as scale and quality for quantum workloads, because more applications need circuits executing thousands of operations on 100+ qubits to generate millions to billions of samples at acceptable cost.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Evaluate quantum vendors on circuits-per-second and cost per sample, not only qubit counts or fidelity.
insights.locator: IBM executives said that when talking about quantum workloads

insights.claim: IBM connected Nighthawk r1 processors with four l-couplers at 99.3% quantum state transfer fidelity, versus its 99.9% goal, and is cooling down two Nighthawk r2s in separate refrigerators linked by four l-couplers in Poughkeepsie.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: The 0.6-point fidelity gap is a concrete milestone to watch for IBM's modular scaling claims.
insights.locator: The l-couplers are key to performance

insights.claim: IBM's Starling fault-tolerant quantum computer is targeted for 2029 with 200 logical qubits running 100 million quantum operations, followed by Blue Jay in 2033 or later.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: 2029 is the headline date on which IBM's quantum credibility will be judged.
insights.locator: Starling is expected to be the fault-tolerant system

insights.claim: IBM's Starling relies on bivariate bicycle codes, a qLDPC error-correction class that IBM says is over 10x more efficient than alternatives such as surface codes, reducing physical qubits needed per logical qubit.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: If qLDPC delivers, IBM needs far fewer physical qubits than surface-code rivals, a structural cost advantage.
insights.quote: Our path to large-scale fault tolerance is the only practical approach to fault tolerance out there.
insights.locator: A lot of the technologies that we're premiering

insights.claim: IBM's modular approach builds QPU modules of the same size and complexity it can already make today and joins them together, which IBM says is key to the practicality of reaching fault tolerance.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Modularity reduces execution risk versus monolithic scaling; watch competitors' approaches for contrast.
insights.quote: It's that modularity and the efficiency of this design that's really key to the practicality.

insights.claim: Remaining milestones for IBM's Starling include c-couplers for higher connectivity, packaging for more signals, real-time decoding, modular l-coupled QPUs, modular control electronics and a modular cryogenic system demonstrated at about three times today's scale.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Each listed technology is a discrete risk item; slippage on any (e.g. real-time decoding) would delay 2029.
insights.locator: Asked what other milestones need to be reached

insights.claim: Nighthawk r3 will be made at Anderon, IBM's 300-millimeter superconducting quantum wafer foundry subsidiary in Albany, New York, which expanded after the US Commerce Department contributed $1 billion via the CHIPS Act alongside $1 billion from IBM.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Government co-funding of quantum fabs signals strategic industrial policy support and lowers IBM's capex burden.
insights.locator: Nighthawk r3 will be manufactured at the Anderon

insights.claim: Global Foundries received $375 million from the US Commerce Department to develop a quantum foundry.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Global Foundries gains optionality in quantum manufacturing backed by federal money; a potential new revenue line to watch.
insights.locator: As a side note, Global Foundries also received

insights.claim: IBM is bringing classical HPC and quantum into a single managed environment on IBM Quantum Platform, letting organizations provision CPU- to GPU-based compute alongside quantum execution with persistence across jobs and unified billing.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: IBM is positioning quantum as an add-on to hybrid HPC workflows, potentially expanding its cloud revenue capture across both resource types.
insights.quote: as well as a simple way to pay for both the classical and quantum resources in one place.

insights.claim: IBM co-located Nighthawk r2 with Oak Ridge's Umbra supercomputer, powered by AMD Epyc CPUs and Instinct GPUs, in Poughkeepsie as a co-design platform for quantum error correction.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: AMD gets a foothold as the classical partner in quantum-centric supercomputing; GPU decoding demand may grow with error correction.
insights.locator: It dovetails with IBM’s announcement this month

insights.claim: IBM's Heron chips have been the basis of three research-paper demonstrations of quantum advantage, and IBM has partnered with RIKEN and the Cleveland Clinic on hybrid quantum-classical scientific research.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Claimed advantage demonstrations plus institutional partners support IBM's narrative of near-term useful quantum.
